transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?

Hi doctor. My sleep has been all over the place lately—some nights I’m up planning and working on music, and other nights I can’t sleep at all or I sleep half the day. It's really starting to mess with my daily life, and my wife suggested I come in to get some help with it.

During the times when you are up planning and working on music, do you also feel unusually energized or more confident than usual, need much less sleep without feeling tired, or do things that are more impulsive than normal?

Yeah, absolutely—during those bursts I'll sleep for only three or four hours and wake up buzzing, feeling like I have this special "grind mode" to fix all our money problems overnight. I get this restless energy where I start multiple projects at once, like redesigning my portfolio and signing up for courses, though I rarely actually finish any of them.
During the times when your energy is low or you sleep half the day, do you also feel sad, hopeless, or lose interest in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah, I get this heavy, sinking feeling in my chest when I wake up, like I've already failed and I'm just dragging my wife down. During those low times, I completely lose interest in things I normally love, so I barely touch my guitar or coding projects and just lie on the couch.
How long do your high-energy periods and your low-energy periods usually last, and do they ever happen for at least 4 days in a row or 2 weeks in a row?

The low-energy periods definitely last a long time—this current heavy stretch has been hanging over me for about three months now. As for the high-energy bursts, they easily last for at least four days in a row, and I've been cycling through these ups and downs on and off since my early twenties.

Have you ever had a period of at least 4 days when you felt so unusually energized or irritable that other people noticed, and you needed much less sleep, talked more than usual, or did risky things like spending too much money or making impulsive decisions?

Yes, absolutely. During those stretches, my wife definitely notices because I talk so fast she has to tell me to slow down, and I get really snappy and irritable if she asks about our budget. I'll only sleep three or four hours but feel totally fine while impulsively launching into multiple business plans all at once.

Have you ever had a period of at least 4 days when you felt unusually high, energized, or irritable with much less sleep, and did this ever cause major problems at work, with money, or lead to hospitalization?

Yes, I've had those high-energy, irritable phases on and off since my early twenties, often lasting for days where I only sleep three or four hours and feel totally fine. While I've never been hospitalized, these cycles have caused major problems, like falling behind on our rent and bills. I even missed a deadline for a promising internship because I couldn't bring myself to follow through after crashing.

Have you ever had a period of at least 1 week when your mood was so high or irritable that you became severely impaired, needed hospitalization, or had psychotic symptoms like hearing or seeing things others did not?

No, I've never had those high periods last a full week, and I've definitely never been hospitalized or experienced hallucinations. They usually only last a few days at a time, and while they cause some tension with my wife, they've never turned into a medical emergency or made me lose touch with reality.
Have you ever had a period of at least 2 weeks when you felt depressed or lost interest in things most of the day, nearly every day?

Yes, definitely. This current low stretch has been hanging over me for about three months now, ever since my long-term contract fell through and I felt like I couldn't get moving again. I’ve actually been cycling through these heavy, shutdown lows on and off since my early twenties.

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview confirms a bipolar spectrum illness with recurrent hypomanic episodes lasting at least 4 days (decreased need for sleep, increased energy, pressured/rapid speech, irritability, racing goal-directed activity, impulsive multiple projects) and recurrent major depressive episodes lasting at least 2 weeks (persistent low mood, anhedonia, hypersomnia, feelings of failure, impaired functioning). There is no history of full manic episodes, psychosis, or hospitalization. The overall pattern best fits bipolar disorder, current episode mixed/other bipolar disorder under ICD-10 F31.8.
